mode: verbatim ingest, hybrid backend (sqlite keyword + embedding bge-m3, probabilistic-OR fusion), default recall stages, no LLM, precise recall profile
how: config.build_gateway(dict); HybridBackend.put_many([(text, id, date)]) once for all memories (written to both children under the memory id); Gateway.recall('owner', {'query': q}) for deployed; HybridBackend.find(query, 10) for ranked
notes: Backend is the hybrid backend: a sqlite keyword child (IDF-weighted containment of character bigrams and CJK single characters) and an embedding child (bge-m3, cosine mapped with floor 0.40 and ceil 0.80); fused score = 1 - prod(1 - score_i) with both weights 1.0. Defaults chosen on the development sets, not on this data.
ranked scores are the fused relevance values, not comparable across systems.

deployed uses the default recall stages with [recall] profile = 'precise' pinned (min_score with the hybrid's precise line 0.70, relative_score with its ratio 0.85, fill_text, drop_oversize, redact, dedupe, budget) and the default limit of 5; ms times that Gateway.recall call only. The plain run of this backend uses the broad lines 0.40 and 0.65 instead. The recall call asks both children, one after the other.

Precise profile: [recall] profile = 'precise': min_score 0.70 and ratio 0.85 (the hybrid's default_min_score and default_relative_ratio, the precise lines) instead of the broad 0.40 and 0.65 of the plain run.
Deployed items are reported by the id field of each recall item; 0 item(s) named no dataset memory.
0 recall call(s) did not answer 200; 0 ranked search(es) failed.
deployed was timed before ranked, so ms includes the real query embedding request; ranked then reuses the backend's query-embedding cache.
Gateway.recall was called directly, so the per-client rate limiter (applied only in admit) was not involved.
Memories were ingested with one put_many call (embedding requests of 32 texts); ingest_seconds covers it.
